newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks head lower in morning after firm start.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks head lower in morning after firm start.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded lower in Tuesday morning trade, unable to hold onto initial gains as shares in HSBC Holdings Plc ran into selling pressure following their recent record run, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was down 11.18 points, or 0.08 percent, at 13,976.62 after rising to an early high of 14,019.03.
Turnover was HK$4.56 billion after the first hour of trade.
HSBC was down HK$1.00 at HK$217.00 after hitting a record high of HK$220.00 on Monday.
"HSBC fell and other property stocks eased between one to two spreads and it seems that the market is looking for a consolidation," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
"The market seems unwilling to decisively breach the psychological barrier of 14,000 and now we are waiting to see whether utilities can lift the market up," Li added.
